title: The underlying manifold of a low-volume hyperbolic 3-orbifold
summary: This paper proves strong restrictions on the underlying topological space of a closed, orientable hyperbolic 3-orbifold \orbM whose volume satisfies a certain upper bound. For instance, if vol(\orbM) < 0.1491, then the underlying space of \orbM must be either a small Seifert fibered space, or the connected sum of two lens spaces (or of a lens space with S^2 x S^1), or the gluing of one or two highly restricted Seifert fibered spaces along a single incompressible torus. If vol(\orbM) < 0.1571 and the singular locus of \orbM is a link, then the topology of the underlying space is restricted…
